# L07: The Most Valuable Marketing Training You'll Ever Watch

Oren John (orenmeetsworld) · youtube · https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=daCB1kVOtMA · notes: [lessons/07_oren-marketing-training.md](../../brain/lessons/07_oren-marketing-training.md)

**Core lesson:** Distribution is king: own a clear position, win free attention with shareable organic formats measured monthly, and move that attention through a funnel close to the money.


## Ideas from this source (54)

- **[Hook = title + verbal + visual](../topics/hooks.md#hook-title-verbal-visual)** · hooks: Analyse every reference by its title hook, verbal hook and visual hook, plus its narrative framework and a simple outline.
- **[Promise a numbered list or a download](../topics/story.md#story-promised-list-open-loop)** · story: A numbered promise ("5 frameworks") or a companion download promised throughout keeps an open loop across a long video.
- **[Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline)** · story: Simple outline Oren uses all the time: controversial question → rapid-fire opinions → justifications → punchline. Reliable mechanisms: "blitz" rapid-fire lists ("10 out of 10 niche habits…") and storytime.
- **[Answer objections inside the content](../topics/story.md#story-answer-objections)** · story: Mine comments (and sales calls) for recurring objections and answer them in future content, like a video sales letter; Oren summarises call objections weekly and feeds them back into content.
- **[Copy only true outliers](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-outliers-vs-own-average)** · ideas: A video is an outlier only against that creator's own average (20K isn't an outlier if they average 100K). Briar keeps a second TikTok account that follows only the niche; Oren's library sorts by ≥2× outliers.
- **[You compete with the whole feed](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-compete-with-feed)** · ideas: Your rivals are everything in the viewer's feed (skits, funny and relatable people), not niche competitors; look outside your niche. Build an account that follows what your ideal viewer follows and check it 10–15 min a day for a couple of weeks.
- **[Shareability: why would they send it?](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-shareability-test)** · ideas: The key test is whether someone would send it to someone else (relatable, expertise, tutorial, funny, interesting, beautiful). Our playbook ranks sends per reach as the strongest signal for reaching new people.
- **[Faceless works if there's a concept](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-faceless-with-concept)** · ideas: No face is needed if there is a concept: POV hands-only skits with voiceover took Gel Blaster's Mexico TikTok to 800,000.
- **[Axial jump cuts every 3–6 words](../topics/editing.md#edit-axial-jump-cuts)** · editing: Talking head: cut from the medium shot to a digital punch-in on the same angle every 3–6 words to hit emphasis words.
- **[Long-form talking pace 2.5–4.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-long-form-talking-pace)** · editing: Long-form talking shots averaged 2.5–3.5 s (Oren's yapping guide) and 2.5–4.5 s in his marketing course, with 8–15 s demo holds and real brand examples as overlays, mockups or split-screens every 10–15 s.
- **[Speed ramps: dead time, beats, top rep](../topics/editing.md#edit-speed-ramps)** · editing: Subtle ramps on browser scrolls and screen recordings remove dead time (L07); the L08 teaser syncs ramps to percussive hits; our gym default ramps into the top rep.
- **[Screen content with a circular face cam](../topics/editing.md#edit-screen-card-circle-facecam)** · editing: Screen recordings fill the frame with a circular face cam: Rahul bottom-centre with a yellow ring and an app-logo badge; Oren in dark rounded cards with drop shadows plus a floating circular PiP camera.
- **[Show proof on screen](../topics/editing.md#edit-proof-inserts)** · editing: Rahul inserts article, doc and GitHub screenshots with yellow highlighter on the key line; Oren runs live tool walkthroughs as proof.
- **[A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event)** · sound: An edit without SFX feels like a "silent movie": put a pop, click, whoosh or snap on every visual change.
- **[SFX meanings: whoosh, pop, chime, thud](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-meaning-map)** · sound: Whoosh for movement (slides, wipes, push-ins, window slide-ins), pop for text in, chime for a green check, thud or click for impact or a card change.
- **[Keyboard clicks and UI pops on bullets](../topics/sound.md#sound-ui-clicks-bullets)** · sound: UI clicks on screen recordings (L06); mechanical keyboard clicks, UI bubble pops and switch clicks on bullets and badges (L07).
- **[Chapter sounds: risers, booms, set foley](../topics/sound.md#sound-riser-sub-boom-chapters)** · sound: Risers and sub-boom impacts at chapter starts and ends; CRT degauss/static on chapter cards; marker squeaks during whiteboard segments.
- **[Music changes by section](../topics/sound.md#sound-music-by-section)** · sound: Driving synthwave with sub-bass for the hook, lo-fi under teaching, deep house for tactics, then an emotional swell into a clean cut at the outro; L06's music also rises at the outro.
- **[Broadcast voice: compress, de-ess, high-pass](../topics/sound.md#sound-broadcast-voice-chain)** · sound: Close mic, tight compression, heavy de-essing, high-pass filter, air boost around 10–12 kHz, proximity low end, room reverb removed.
- **[Bigger 1.15–1.3× punch-ins on punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-big-punch-in)** · effects: Smooth 1.15–1.3× punch-ins on punchlines and framework declarations, bigger than L06's.
- **[Entrances ease out, exits ease in](../topics/effects.md#fx-ease-out-entrances)** · effects: Things that arrive ease out (fast, then a long brake, "as if set down by a steady hand"); things that leave ease in (slow start, then away). Oren's overlays slide in with spring/ease-out.
- **[UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot](../topics/effects.md#fx-spring-ui)** · effects: Interface elements and text pops use a spring that overshoots its target a little, then settles (spring/bounce slide-ins in L02; spring UI cards in L07).
- **[Kinetic type: float-ins, glow, pop-ins](../topics/effects.md#fx-kinetic-words)** · effects: Spoken keywords float in as kinetic text (L07); the L08 teaser adds outer glow, chromatic aberration, scale pop-ins and tracked floating text with cubic-bezier easing.
- **[Horizontal wipes and slide-ins](../topics/transitions.md#tr-kinetic-wipes)** · transitions: Kinetic text slide-ins and horizontal wipes move between ideas, each with a whoosh.
- **[Chapter cards: chrome emblem, CRT static](../topics/transitions.md#tr-crt-static-chapter)** · transitions: Each chapter opens with a 3D chrome emblem on a CRT TV that comes in on a static burst.
- **[Extended bold sans titles, neon highlights](../topics/text.md#text-extended-sans-neon)** · text: Extended bold geometric sans titles (Druk Wide / Monument Extended style) + Inter/Neue Haas body; white on dark with cyan, lime and neon-pink highlights on numbers and acronyms.
- **[Four copy styles](../topics/text.md#text-four-copy-styles)** · text: Direct response (urgent, numbers, confrontational; Oren's "highest efficacy"), evidence-led (testimonials, calm), human/story-driven, culturally savvy (pop-culture wordplay).
- **[High contrast, deep blacks, neon accents](../topics/colour.md#colour-neon-high-contrast)** · colour: The marketing course: high contrast, deep blacks, saturated neon accents (cyan, magenta, amber/tungsten).
- **[Treat places as sets](../topics/filming.md#film-sets-evergreen-temporary)** · filming: Evergreen sets (office corner, warehouse, studio day) and temporary ones (a booth the night before). Oren's course rotates 6 physical sets every few minutes as pattern interrupts.
- **[Talking-head light and lens looks](../topics/filming.md#film-talking-head-lighting)** · filming: Soft key front-left with a 35–50 mm wide-aperture look (L06); warm key with gold rim (L01); 20–24 mm wide for energy (L07); high-key soft 3-point with rim for a podcast (L08).
- **[TikTok: more candid, shot on iPhone](../topics/filming.md#film-tiktok-candid-iphone)** · filming: Oren's per-network strategy makes TikTok content more personal and candid, shot on iPhone.
- **[Positioning: known for, shelf test](../topics/brand.md#brand-positioning-known-for)** · brand: Positioning is what you're known for: not generic, remembered, AI-legible. Shelf test: stand next to everyone in the category and name your reason to exist (Monster = counterculture, Celsius = health).
- **[Positioning type and one statement](../topics/brand.md#brand-positioning-types)** · brand: Pick one type (performance, category creation, counter, smart, value, niche, generational, single attribute, premium, counter-luxury, name) as north star; write "For [target] who [need], [brand] is the [category] that [benefit]. Unlike [competitor], we [differentiator]."
- **[Brand world: characters, sets, plot](../topics/brand.md#brand-world-characters-sets)** · brand: Map who can be on camera and every set, then plot it like TV: events, enemies (competitor moves), friends (partners to piggyback), specials (your own series for empty stretches); find the holes and refresh monthly.
- **[Events calendar: personal, culture, industry](../topics/brand.md#brand-events-calendar)** · brand: A calendar by month or quarter of company/personal events, culture moments (New Year, summer, Black Friday) and industry events (CES, competitor launches).
- **[Three Instagram strategies](../topics/brand.md#brand-instagram-strategies)** · brand: Expert on camera (Oren's #1, at least 3 posts/week), storytelling about an interesting business (~2/week), or extremely art-directed. People beat brand handles: personalities drive more impact.
- **[CTA to a landing page or email list](../topics/growth.md#growth-cta-to-owned-list)** · growth: Every piece needs an ask, and Oren's points to an owned list: his bio CTA is "join my brand strategy newsletter".
- **[Growth timelines and 1% maths (claims)](../topics/growth.md#growth-one-percent-better)** · growth: Briar: 300 views + 1% a day ≈ 11,400 average views in a year. Oren: traction in 3–5 months of a pillar system. Caleb: 2–3 months of consistency = "top 1%". All their estimates.
- **[Per-post vs account metrics](../topics/growth.md#growth-post-and-account-metrics)** · growth: Per post: hook rate, views, saves, shares. Per account: monthly reach, leads/sign-ups/email adds, sales attributed to social.
- **[Content funnel: top, middle, bottom](../topics/growth.md#growth-content-funnel)** · growth: Top of funnel gets attention and may not mention the product ("raises the floor"); middle educates about you; bottom exists to sell or sign up and gets low views.
- **[Pillar system: 3–5 formats × 3–4 a month](../topics/growth.md#growth-pillar-system)** · growth: Test 3–5 formats, each 3–4 times a month (12–16 posts); review views, saves, shares, hook rate and new vs old followers a couple of days after month end (~1 h); swap a format after two worse months.
- **[Master one network, cross-post the rest](../topics/growth.md#growth-master-one-cross-post)** · growth: Get good at one primary network (usually Instagram) first, cross-post everywhere because it compounds, and build per-network strategies later.
- **[Collab posts bring new audiences](../topics/growth.md#growth-collab-pillar)** · growth: A regular collaborator making about 4 collab posts a month brings a new audience; our Khandala carousel was planned as a Collab with a colleague, and tags add reach via their networks.
- **[Bio in three lines](../topics/growth.md#growth-bio-three-lines)** · growth: Line 1 what you do, line 2 why follow, line 3 a CTA.
- **[Expert content: 3 a week minimum](../topics/growth.md#growth-expert-cadence)** · growth: Expert-on-camera content is "a three times a week kind of minimum"; narrative accounts about 2 a week.
- **[Creator pyramid: micro, mid, anchors](../topics/business.md#biz-creator-pyramid)** · business: Micro creators for volume and ad creative, mid-tier (30K–100K) as the core, a few big anchors on top. Brands pay via ad creative, seeding, affiliates, paid posts and whitelisting.
- **[Whitelisting vs darklisting](../topics/business.md#biz-whitelisting)** · business: Whitelisting: a brand runs the creator's own post as an ad via an ad/partnership code (often outperforms). Darklisting: an ad from the creator's account that never appears on their feed.
- **[Modular brief](../topics/business.md#biz-modular-brief)** · business: Two key messages, target, content type, hook inspiration (text/visual/spoken), references, mechanism, simple outline, assets, variants (CTA versions, 2–3 hooks). The best 10% of creators don't need it.
- **[Ad maths and the Meta test](../topics/business.md#biz-ad-maths)** · business: 3:1 LTV:CAC north star; thumb stop doesn't matter if ROAS hits. Test: one concept per ad set, ~$50/day, lookalikes 3% → 10%, 3–10 distinct ads, spend 3–5× target CPA before judging.
- **[Closer to the dollars, more money](../topics/business.md#biz-closer-to-dollars)** · business: Funnel: attention → CTA → landing page → lead/sale → CRM → fast touches. A landing page removes every buying objection. North stars: page conversion and close rate.
- **[Email 1–3 a week, plain text](../topics/business.md#biz-email-cadence)** · business: Campaigns vs automated flows; 1–3 sends a week, plain text from a person (Oren). Harry: less news, more letter: time-and-place intro, 5–6 examples with conflict, no paragraph over two lines.
- **[Weekly update: wins, next, blockers, numbers](../topics/process.md#proc-weekly-update)** · process: A weekly note up the chain: wins, what's next, blockers, KPIs.
- **[Turn the workflow into a skill](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-turn-into-skill)** · ai-tools: "Hey, turn this into a skill": next time it's one prompt. Oren's levels: chat → project → skills → agents → a "true brain"; repeatable things become skills, with one owner per skill.
- **[Brand project plus a human layer](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-brand-project-human-layer)** · ai-tools: Upload the positioning statement, product info, site copy and testimonials (not big brand guides) to a shared project, give feedback, then add human case studies and nuances on top.
